newsitem.title: CHINA: China waives zinc, lead export tariffs in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China waives zinc, lead export tariffs in 1997.

text.p: China will cut the temporary export tariff on zinc to zero in 1997 from a preferential 5.0 percent this year and retain a zero export tariff on lead, officials of the China Non-Ferrous Metals Export Import Co said on Monday.
An official at the Zhuzhou Smelter in central Hunan province said smelters in China were hoping that the export tariff would be zero for both lead and zinc.
The export tariff rates on lead and tin were zero percent and the rate on zinc was 5.0 percent in 1996.

The export tariff rate for 1997 on lead ores and concentrate was 5.0 percent. The 1997 rate for zinc ores and conentrate would be 10 percent and the rate for tin ores and concentrate 20 percent, the China news service said quoting figures from the State Council Customs Commission.
It gave no details of last year's rates.
